newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour unveils contract with people.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour unveils contract with people.

text.p: Opposition leader Tony Blair, launching the Labour Party's manifesto for a May 1 election, on Thursday made 10 promises in a "contract with the people" to govern Britain from the political centre ground.

A day after the ruling Conservatives launched their policy blueprint, Blair promised not to raise income tax rates, to guarantee low inflation, to get thousands of young people back to work and to show leadership in Europe.

Blair told a news conference that with the publication of the programmes of the two main parties, voters now had a real choice "between the future and the past, between a party for the many and a party for the few, between leadership and drift".
Blair said voters would be able to judge Labour, which has been out of power for 18 years, on whether they fulfilled the 10 pledges.

"We make a virtue of the fact that our manifesto does not promise the earth. It does not say it can do everything. There are no magic wands or instant solutions. What we do say is: "Britain deserves better,'" he said.
Labour is widely tipped to win the election and leads the Conservatives by around 20 points in opinion polls.
